subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap & recommended next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme.com>, Dana Lopez <dana.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap & recommended next steps

Hi Sam / Dana,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and helpful context on the use cases (customer support KB + contract summarization). Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from call:
- Primary use case: short, high-precision answers from internal KB (support articles + contracts).
- Non-functional constraints: 300ms P95 latency target for chat UI; budget sensitivity at scale (500k queries/month).
- Data: mixed-size docs (snippets to full contracts), want strong grounding and low hallucination.

Initial recommendations (high-level):
1) Retriever: dense vector retrieval (FAISS/HNSW) with embeddings from redwood-embedding-1 for domain embedding consistency. k_retriever = 10 as a starting point.
2) Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for high-precision top results (top_k_rerank = 5). If latency budget is tighter, consider a two-stage approach: lightweight lexical filter (BM25) -> dual-encoder -> small cross-encoder for top-5.
3) Generation model options: redwood-13b-quant (best quality/grounding in our benchmarks) OR redwood-3b-flan (lower cost, slightly higher hallucination risk).
4) Grounding metrics to monitor: P@1, grounding rate (fraction of answers citing >=1 doc), and hallucination rate (manual eval sample). Recommend threshold: grounding_score >= 0.7 for answers surfaced to users.

Attached: acme_rag_benchmark_results.pdf (summary of run with k=10, rerank top-5) and prompt_set_v2.csv (current prompt eval set). Also linking our benchmark Drive folder below.

Proposed next steps:
- Nikhil to share more detailed config and latency/cost tradeoffs (attached).
- We can run a short 1k-query pilot across your top-50 docs to validate grounding and latency.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review pilot results.

Would love to confirm: are you okay with the cross-encoder first-pass recommendation, or do you prefer to prioritize latency/cost (we can show a hybrid config)?

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap & recommended next steps

Hey Sam / Dana — quick technical notes based on our internal benchmark runs (attached PDF has full tables):

Short answers & reranker latency:
- Cross-encoder top-5 rerank adds ~110–160ms median per query on an A100 setup in our test harness (this varies with sequence length). Dual-encoder (dot-product) only is ~30–45ms. So expect ~120ms additional median cost for cross-encoder on top-5.
- Cost: cross-encoder is ~2.4x compute vs dual-encoder for the rerank stage.

Recommended config for your constraints (P95 latency ~300ms target):
- Retriever: dense (FAISS HNSW) with dimension 1536 embeddings from redwood-embedding-1. k_retriever = 10.
- Rerank: cross-encoder on top_k_rerank = 5 for high-precision user-facing answers. If you need lower latency, use a hybrid: BM25 filter (top 50) -> dense (top 10) -> cross-encoder (top 5).
- Generation: redwood-13b-quant with constrained decoding (max_tokens 180) for summary answers; fall back to redwood-3b-flan for low-cost bulk operations.
- Grounding threshold: use a combined score (retriever_score_norm * reranker_score_norm) and require >= 0.7 to auto-surface answers. For borderline cases return citations and a "may be incorrect" UI flag.

Benchmark highlights (pilot-sized run, 1k queries):
- P@1: 0.82 (cross-encoder top-5 + redwood-13b-quant)
- Grounding rate: 0.88 (answers with >=1 correct citation in top-3)
- Hallucination rate (manual sample): 6.5%
- End-to-end median latency (retrieval + rerank + gen): ~280ms (A100, batch size 1)

Files attached: acme_rag_benchmark_results.pdf (detailed results by prompt/len) and prompt_set_v2.csv (sanitized prompts used for eval). I've also pasted the example retrieval config below for convenience:
- retriever.k = 10
- retriever.type = dense_faiss_hnsw
- reranker.top_k = 5
- reranker.type = cross_encoder
- grounding.threshold = 0.7

Let us know if you want us to run a short pilot against a sample of your production docs (we can do 1k queries and produce an eval report in 3 business days).

Thanks,
Nikhil
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.com

Thanks Nikhil — that helps a lot. Couple follow-ups from our side: 

1) Regression monitoring: how does Redwood alert on quality drops? Do you support evaluation hooks tied to a prompt set and automatic regression alerts (e.g., if P@1 drops by >5%)? We need to surface this to our ops team.
2) Long-form/legal docs: our contracts are long — will the recommended k=10 + cross-encoder still perform for long-context retrievals? Any different config suggestions for long evidence retrieval?

Neha — adding you here since CS/ops will own the pilot onboarding.

Dana
Senior PM | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme RAG eval - post-call recap & recommended next steps

Appreciate the questions — quick answers and next steps: 

- Regression monitoring: yes — Redwood Optimize supports scheduled eval runs against a saved prompt set and will trigger alerts when key metrics (P@1, grounding_rate) cross thresholds. We can configure a weekly job to run your prompt_set_v2.csv and alert via Slack/email if P@1 drops >5% or hallucination_rate increases >3pp. Neha will own CS onboarding and alert config.
- Long-form documents: for contracts we recommend chunking by semantic sections (prefers 1k–2k token chunks) and increasing retriever.k to 20 for long-context lookups; keep reranker.top_k at 5. We can also add a secondary run with a long-context specialized prompt to extract the most relevant clause.

Next steps / action items:
- Redwood: run a 1k-query pilot against a sanitized sample of your documents (Marissa to get sample + NDA if needed). Deliverable: pilot eval PDF (P@1, grounding_rate, latency, hallucination sample) in 3 business days.
- Acme: share sanitized sample set + any embargoed doc list by EOD Tue (31 May).
- Schedule follow-up: Calendly link (below) — proposing Tue 1 Jun 10:00am PT to review pilot results.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-2027-01
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-example-benchmark
Schedule: https://calendly.com/marissa-cole/redwood-acme-rag-followup

I'll follow up with Neha to kick off the pilot once the sample arrives. Thanks all — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Marissa
